label: Huntington's microbehavior phenotyping pipeline
title: A Pilot Study in Integrated Machine Learning and Kinematic Framework for Automated Behavioral Phenotyping in Mice
one_line: Low-cost open-source ML and kinematic pipeline for phenotyping HD mice.
venue: Journal of Biomedical Engineering and Biosciences
details: A low-cost, open-source analysis pipeline for phenotyping Huntington's disease model mice from video of novel-object exploration. It combines DeepLabCut pose estimation, manual annotation in BORIS and A-SOiD behavior classification with a custom Python framework that turns keypoint trajectories into measures of locomotion, stationary time and object interaction. It was tested on a small pilot cohort, so genotype differences are preliminary.

title: ABEL: an active-learning behavior estimation and labeling platform
one_line: Active-learning platform for behavior estimation and labeling
details: Open-source platform for annotating and estimating animal behavior that uses active learning to decide which samples a user should label next. It aims to cut the manual labeling effort needed to train supervised behavior classifiers.

label: Pain behavior recognition model
title: AI-powered rodent behavior recognition model for pain research
one_line: AI behavior recognition model for pain research
details: AI-based model for recognizing rodent behaviors relevant to pain research. It is intended to automate the scoring of pain-related behavior from recordings of rats or mice, reducing reliance on manual observation.

label: Lionfish behavior classifier
title: Applying machine learning tools for automated behaviour classification in invasive lionfish and comparison with human observations
one_line: ML classifiers for automated lionfish behaviour, validated against human observers.
details: Machine-learning classifiers that automatically score behavior of invasive lionfish from video, with outputs compared against scoring by human observers. Code and materials are openly archived, making it a reference for applying automated behavior classification to marine fish.

title: Autobehaver: An AI-Based Pipeline for Animal Behavior Analysis
one_line: AI pipeline for animal behavior analysis
details: Pipeline for high-throughput phenotyping of individual Drosophila filmed on a low-cost recording rig. Keypoints are extracted from each video, a Transformer labels behavior and orientation frame by frame, and the results are summarized as per-animal feature vectors. Gradient-boosted ensembles then separate experimental groups, and SHAP-based feature importance shows which behavioral measures drive the differences, giving an interpretable comparison of genotypes or conditions.

label: NORT YOLOv11 framework
title: Automated behavior analysis in the novel object recognition test
one_line: YOLOv11 pose + frame classifiers and heuristics to score novel object recognition tests
details: Open-source framework for scoring the novel object recognition test in rats from video. It combines YOLOv11 pose estimation, frame-level classifiers and rule-based heuristics to detect object exploration, with the trial annotations released alongside the code.

label: Cavefish aggression classifier
title: Automated Profiling of Social Behaviors to Assess the Genetic Basis of Evolution of Aggressive Behaviors in Astyanax mexicanus
one_line: Pose + supervised pipeline scoring striking, following, circling in cavefish.
venue: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A Ecological and Integrative Physiology
details: Machine-learning pipeline that tracks multiple Mexican tetra (Astyanax mexicanus) in video and uses supervised classifiers to score aggression-related behaviors: striking, following and circling. It was used to compare surface fish, cavefish and their hybrids at juvenile stages, supporting genetic studies of how social behavior evolves. Data and code are openly archived.

title: B-REAL: A keypoint-less behavior platform for offline classification and real-time detection
one_line: Pose-free classifier for offline and real-time behavior detection
details: Pose-free behavior classifier that maps raw video directly to behavior labels, skipping the need to train a keypoint model first. Inference runs faster than video frame rate even on a CPU, so detections can trigger stimuli, rewards or other manipulations in closed-loop experiments. It needs relatively little labeled data, can be pretrained on unlabeled video, and has been demonstrated on rodent and fly datasets.

title: Animal behavioral analysis and neural encoding with transformer-based self-supervised pretraining
one_line: Self-supervised vision-transformer pretraining (masked autoencoding + temporal contrastive) for pose, action segmentation and neural encoding
details: Self-supervised pretraining approach that learns vision-transformer representations from unlabeled animal behavior video, combining masked autoencoding with a temporal contrastive objective. The learned features can be reused for pose estimation, action segmentation and encoding of neural activity across multiple species.

title: BehaVERT: A Transformer-Based Motion Language Model for Decoding Behavioral Semantics in Mice
one_line: Transformer motion-language model decoding behavioral semantics from skeleton
details: Transformer model for mice that treats skeletal keypoint trajectories like language, tokenizing movement into units and learning temporal structure to decode behavior. It handles both discrete behavior labels and continuous state classification, and includes web-based annotation tools for keypoints and behaviors that require no programming. Attention maps and clustering of learned representations help interpret which moments drive predictions; curated benchmark annotations are also provided.

title: BehaviorScope-X: reusing pose-trained visual representations for full-video ethology
one_line: Reuses pose-network visual features for full-video ethology
details: Behavior classification workflow that reuses an already trained pose model as a visual encoder. The pose network is run once to cache detections, keypoints, social geometry and internal image features, and lightweight temporal classifiers are then trained on these cached windows. It works with several pose backbones, including DeepLabCut SuperAnimal models, has been tested on mouse resident-intruder and fly aggression videos, and can run near or at real time on consumer hardware.

label: Frame-wise CNN classifier
title: Classifying rodent behaviors one frame at a time: A CNN-based method
one_line: Frame-by-frame CNN behavior classification with image dataset
details: Convolutional neural network approach that classifies rodent behavior from individual video frames, without pose estimation, body-part segmentation or temporal context. Only frame-level labels are needed, and the method is accompanied by a large image dataset of rodent behaviors recorded in operant conditioning chambers. It can be applied to static images as well as partial video recordings.

title: DairySocialTwin: Auditable Video Analytics for Dairy Digital Twins
one_line: Auditable video analytics for dairy-cow social behavior digital twins
details: Open-source video analytics framework for monitoring social behavior of dairy cows, designed to feed digital-twin models of the herd. Its emphasis is on auditable, traceable outputs from barn video.

title: A community benchmark enables high-resolution, cross-lab quantification of mouse social behavior
one_line: Cross-lab annotated social behavior benchmark with community challenge
details: Benchmark of manually annotated video and pose tracking of mouse social and solitary behaviors, pooled from 15 laboratories and covering 33 behaviors, originally released through a community classification challenge. Building on challenge entries, the accompanying HiDRA classifier is designed to generalize to labs not seen in training. Both the dataset and the classifiers are released as open resources.

label: ActionFormer for mice
title: Decoding Self-paced Activity in Mice with ActionFormer
one_line: Adapts ActionFormer transformer for mouse action localization
venue: Communications in computer and information science
details: Adaptation of the ActionFormer transformer, a temporal action localization model, to video of mice in the locomotor activity test. Rather than summary metrics such as distance traveled, it localizes the timing of common spontaneous behaviors and summarizes them as behavior signatures that can reveal drug effects, group differences and dose-response relationships.

title: A promptable foundation model enables automated multi-task dataset construction and real-time pose estimation in mice
one_line: Promptable foundation model for dataset building and real-time pose
details: Pose-estimation pipeline for groups of interacting mice that first segments and tracks each animal from a text prompt with the SAM 3 foundation model, then runs a DeepLabCut pretrained pose network restricted to each mask. This reduces keypoints being assigned to the wrong animal during crowding and occlusion. It was used to build a multi-assay mouse dataset with boxes, masks, identities and poses, and to train a lightweight pose model that runs faster than video acquisition.

title: DiverScan: attention-guided exploratory analysis of animal behaviour across diverse comparative experiments
one_line: Attention-guided exploratory comparison of behavioral tracking data
details: Deep-learning framework for exploratory comparison of behavioral time series from tracking data, for example control versus treatment groups. An attention-based architecture highlights which behavioral features differ between conditions, and a large language model generates explanatory text. It accepts flexible input formats, handles single- and multi-animal data across species, and is distributed as Jupyter notebooks with a graphical interface.

label: Barbary macaque detection dataset
title: Enhancing wildlife monitoring with computer vision: A dataset for automated detection of barbary macaques
one_line: Annotated image dataset for automated detection of wild Barbary macaques
details: Image dataset (MagotSeg) for automated detection of Barbary macaques, collected from multiple zoo cameras across times of day and seasons. Annotations include instance segmentation masks and an age-class label for each animal, and the data were used to train and compare YOLO detection models for primate monitoring.

title: EthoTrace: from behaviour to neural dynamics in a unified analysis system
one_line: Unified system linking behavior to neural dynamics
details: Browser-based tool, delivered as a single self-contained HTML file that runs offline without installation, for linking behavior annotations to fiber photometry calcium signals. Users score behavior on a timeline shared with the dF/F trace, correct and normalize the signal, inspect individual bouts and align repeated bouts for statistical comparison, all in one session. It suits self-initiated behaviors such as parenting or social interaction that lack an external trigger.

one_line: Automated mouse grimace scoring for tracking pain over time
details: Open-source extension of the LabGym platform that scores pain-related facial expressions in freely moving mice from ordinary video, without manual frame selection or restrictive imaging setups. It tracks ear, eye and nose movements frame by frame and combines them into a weighted composite pain score, producing continuous measures of pain over time based on the Mouse Grimace Scale concept.

label: Residual-guided visual context
title: Learning When Visual Context Matters for Mouse Behavior Analysis
one_line: Pose motion encoder that adds video features only on frames where pose is insufficient
details: Mouse behavior analysis framework (ResiFuse) built on a pose-based motion encoder that adds video-derived visual context only on frames where pose alone is a poor fit. It uses the encoder's quantization residuals to pick those frames, giving the benefit of visual information without processing every frame. It supports both supervised behavior classification and unsupervised segmentation, with the largest gains on socially complex data.

label: Facial pain videography analysis
title: Manual and automated capture of analgesic-responsive facial pain behaviors of unrestrained mice in a trigeminal neuralgia model
one_line: High-frame-rate video analysis of spontaneous and evoked facial pain behaviors.
details: Open-source analysis approach for facial pain behavior in unrestrained mice in a trigeminal neuralgia model, using high-frame-rate video. It quantifies spontaneous asymmetric grooming and mechanically evoked facial rubbing, and uses DeepLabCut tracking to measure head-movement speed after facial stimulation, yielding readouts that respond to analgesics such as carbamazepine.

title: Developmental Dynamics of Naturalistic Social Behavior Revealed by Longitudinal Multi-Animal Tracking
one_line: Multi-animal pose estimation with video object segmentation for stable identities in home-cage groups
details: Multi-animal pose-estimation pipeline (Move-Altogether) that combines video object segmentation with contour-guided preprocessing to keep identities stable when group-housed mice overlap. The resulting pose sequences feed a denoising-autoencoder framework that maps home-cage social behavior, such as spacing, orientation and interaction dynamics, into a low-dimensional space for longitudinal comparison, including mother-pup interactions.

title: MSGL-Transformer: A Multi-Scale Global-Local Transformer for Rodent Social Behavior Recognition
one_line: Multi-scale global-local transformer on pose for rodent social behavior recognition
details: Transformer model that recognizes rodent social behaviors from pose keypoint sequences. Parallel attention branches capture short-, medium- and long-range temporal dynamics, and a modulation block emphasizes behavior-relevant features. The same architecture was applied to rat (RatSI) and mouse (CalMS21) datasets by changing only the input size and number of classes.

label: Multi-scale autoencoder for social behavior
title: Multi-scale autoencoder-based unsupervised framework for social behavioral structure discovery and anomaly detection
one_line: Unsupervised multi-scale autoencoder for discovering social behavior structure and anomalies
venue: SICE Journal of Control Measurement and System Integration
details: Unsupervised framework that learns typical mouse social behavior from pose trajectories using an LSTM autoencoder operating at multiple time scales. Trained on control animals, it scores deviations as anomalies in other groups, such as mice reared under different conditions, without requiring hand-defined behaviors like nose-to-nose contact.

label: Intermediate-representation benchmark
title: Optimizing Intermediate Representations: A Framework for Low-Cost, High-Accuracy Behavior Quantification
one_line: Benchmark of keypoint density, features and segmentation shapes as inputs for behavior classifiers
details: Benchmark study comparing the intermediate representations used as inputs to supervised mouse behavior classifiers. It tests how classification depends on the number of pose keypoints, on temporal features such as FFT-based signals, and on shape descriptors from whole-body segmentation, offering guidance on where annotation effort pays off.

title: PoseR: a deep learning toolbox for classifying animal behaviour
one_line: Deep learning toolbox classifying behavior from pose
details: Open-source deep-learning toolbox that classifies behavior directly from pose-estimation output using spatio-temporal graph convolutional networks, avoiding species- or task-specific feature engineering. It converts keypoint coordinates into behavior labels and has been applied to zebrafish larvae, Drosophila, mice and rats.

label: Nematode aggression state model
title: Predatory aggression evolved through adaptations to noradrenergic circuits
one_line: ML model from tracking identifies aggressive behavioural states in predatory nematodes.
details: Machine-learning model built on behavioral tracking data from the predatory nematode Pristionchus pacificus that identifies recurring behavioral states, including aggressive predatory bouts and passive states. The open-source code allows these states to be quantified when testing genetic or neuromodulatory manipulations.

label: Space-experiment behavior detector
title: Research on Animal Behavior Detection System for Space Science Experiments
one_line: YOLO segmentation tracking plus behavior recognition for in-orbit videos
details: Behavior monitoring system for animal videos recorded during space missions. It uses YOLOv11n-seg instance segmentation to track multiple animals and extract trajectories and interactions, then applies task-specific rules to flag behaviors of interest such as abnormal aggregation or prolonged immobility in real time. It was developed with a fruit fly segmentation dataset from the China Space Station.

title: SingleBehavior Lab: behavioral sequencing and phenotyping with lightweight task specific adaptation
one_line: Behavioral sequencing and phenotyping with lightweight task-specific adaptation
details: Framework with a graphical interface that models behavior from video using embeddings from large pretrained video foundation models, with small adapters trained on top so only a few labeled examples are needed. It supports action segmentation and classification, plus unsupervised clustering of behavioral states using object-centered features from a segmentation model, with tools for transition analysis and interpretability. Applicable across assays and species.

title: Smart Monkey Lab: a scalable AI-based individualfacial identification for Japanese macaques
one_line: AI facial identification of individual Japanese macaques
details: AI-based system for recognizing individual Japanese macaques from their faces, intended to scale identification of monkeys in research settings.

label: Olfactory habituation scoring pipeline
title: Using Machine Learning to Automate the Analysis of an Olfactory Habituation‐Dishabituation Task in Mice
one_line: Automated side-view pipeline scoring olfactory habituation-dishabituation task performance.
details: Open-source pipeline that automates scoring of the mouse olfactory habituation-dishabituation task from a single side-view camera. DeepLabCut provides pose estimation and SimBA classifies odor interaction, yielding sniffing time for water, familiar and novel social odors. Results were validated against manual annotation.

title: V-TRACE: End-to-end temporal inference and annotation of animal behaviors from video
one_line: End-to-end video-based temporal behavior inference and annotation
details: End-to-end method with a graphical interface that detects and annotates animal behavior directly from raw video, without pose keypoints as an intermediate step. A self-supervised pretrained video transformer with multi-scale temporal modeling predicts both what behavior occurs and its start and end times. It has been tested on datasets from several species and experimental setups.

title: VECTR-Clasp: An open machine learning and vector-based framework for objective quantification of hind-limb clasping and motor dysfunction in Cdkl5 -deficient mice
one_line: ML vector-based quantification of hind-limb clasping
details: Open-source framework for the mouse hind-limb clasping test that combines DeepLabCut pose estimation and SimBA classification to detect clasping, then computes continuous body-relative geometric measures such as head direction, distance traveled and swing count. These go beyond categorical observer scores and can reveal subtle motor phenotypes, demonstrated in a Cdkl5-deficient mouse model.

title: Versatile night/day framework for longitudinal Pi-based Imaging (VeNFLoPi) is an open-source camera setup for behavioral assays
one_line: Open-source Raspberry Pi day/night camera setup
details: Open-source Raspberry Pi camera system for long-term behavioral recording in both light and dark conditions. It combines Pi cameras, custom infrared lighting, 3D-printed mounts and centralized recording through OBS, with fisheye correction and optional scripts for timestamping and stitching. It needs no custom coding and outputs video ready for tools such as DeepLabCut and LabGym.

title: YORU: Animal behavior detection with object-based approach for real-time closed-loop feedback
one_line: Object-detection behavior recognition for real-time closed-loop feedback
details: Open-source behavior detection tool that uses a deep-learning object detector to recognize behaviors directly as objects in each frame, based on animal shape, rather than through pose estimation. It handles social behaviors among multiple individuals, from insects to vertebrates, and runs in real time, enabling closed-loop feedback such as photostimulation targeted to specific individuals.

label: Circadian behavior suite
title: A circadian behavioral analysis suite for real-time classification of daily rhythms in complex behaviors
one_line: Continuous real-time self-supervised behavior classification of daily rhythms
details: Open-source package (CBAS) for continuous, long-term recording and real-time classification of complex home-cage behaviors in multiple mice in parallel. It uses a self-supervised computer vision model to classify behaviors such as digging and nesting, enabling circadian analysis of behaviors that are hard to measure with conventional sensors.

label: Open-source olfactometer
title: A low-cost and open-source olfactometer to precisely deliver single odours and odour mixtures
one_line: Low-cost open-source olfactometer for odour and mixture delivery
details: Low-cost, fully open-source olfactometer for delivering single odors and odor mixtures with controlled timing. It can be built without a machine shop or specialized engineering skills, and full design and assembly details are provided. It has been validated in both rodent behavior experiments and human psychophysics.

label: Disgust reaction counter
title: Automatic quantification of disgust reactions in mice using machine learning
one_line: Machine-learning method to automatically count taste-elicited disgust reactions.
details: Method for automatically counting taste-elicited disgust reactions in mice from video. DeepLabCut tracks the nose and paws, and a random forest classifier trained on manually labeled examples detects disgust reactions and their type, supporting large-scale taste reactivity testing.

title: A machine learning tool with light-based image analysis for automatic classification of 3D pain behaviors
one_line: ML with light-based imaging classifying 3D pain behaviors like paw flinching
details: Open-source supervised classifier (ARBEL) for pain-related behaviors in freely moving mice recorded from below. It combines pose estimation with light-based image analysis that estimates paw pressure and distance from the floor, allowing behaviors such as paw flinching to be scored in three dimensions. Suited to extended recordings and drug screening.

title: An autonomous AI agent for universal behavior analysis
one_line: Autonomous multimodal AI agent automating video behavior analysis
details: Autonomous AI agent that analyzes behavior videos without task-specific training or manual annotation. Built on large language and vision-language models, it identifies the experimental paradigm, picks subjects and objects to track, performs tracking, pose estimation and segmentation, writes and runs analysis code, and produces a research report with its reasoning shown. Demonstrated across plants, insects, rodents, primates and humans.

title: BL-BERT: Extracting Body Language from Behavior Sequences in Freely Moving Mice
one_line: BERT-style model extracting body language from behavior sequences
venue: Communications in computer and information science
details: BL-BERT applies a BERT-style language model to sequences of behavior from freely moving mice. It treats behavior sequences like text to extract recurring body-language patterns without predefined labels.

title: CASTLE: a training-free foundation-model pipeline for cross-species behavioral classification
one_line: Training-free foundation-model pipeline for cross-species behavior classification
details: A pipeline that classifies behavior from raw video without training any task-specific model. It chains pretrained foundation models to segment and track each animal, then extracts orientation-invariant image features from the masked animal region. An interactive module lets users cluster these embeddings hierarchically while viewing the underlying frames, so behavior categories can be discovered without predefined labels. It has been demonstrated on mice, Drosophila and C. elegans.

label: Social interaction composite index
title: Classification of social behavioral responses in stress and non-stress adult male mice with high precision
one_line: Bidimensional index combining interaction ratio and aggressor distance for social stress.
details: An analysis framework for the mouse social interaction test used in social-stress studies. It combines the usual time-in-zone interaction ratio with the continuous average distance to the CD1 aggressor, giving a two-dimensional index that separates mice that enter the zone but keep their distance from those that approach closely. It builds on pose tracking from DeepLabCut and DeepOF.

title: Cross-Skeleton Interaction Graph Aggregation Network for Representation Learning of Mouse Social Behavior
one_line: Cross-skeleton graph network for mouse social behavior representation
details: A graph neural network that learns representations of social behavior between freely interacting mice from pose keypoints. It models interactions within each skeleton, between skeletons and across body parts of different animals, and uses an interaction-aware transformer plus an auxiliary self-supervised task to classify social behaviors. It was evaluated on skeleton versions of the CRIM13 dataset and a new mouse dataset.

title: DIPLOMAT: multi-animal tracking with efficient manual editing
one_line: Multi-animal pose tracking with identity maintenance and efficient manual editing
details: A multi-animal pose tracker that builds on the per-frame body-part predictions of DeepLabCut or SLEAP models. Instead of taking the single most likely location in each frame, it splits the probability maps among the tracked animals and uses across-frame movement and body-part distances to keep identities consistent through occlusions. The retained probabilities feed a manual editing interface that lets users re-track several body parts at once with little effort.

title: DLC2Action: a deep learning-based toolbox for automated behavior segmentation
one_line: Deep-learning toolbox for automated behavior segmentation from pose (Mathis lab)

label: Unsupervised behavior benchmark
title: Evaluation of unsupervised learning algorithms for the classification of behavior from pose estimation data
one_line: Benchmarks unsupervised algorithms for classifying behavior from pose data.
details: An open benchmark comparing unsupervised learning algorithms for classifying rodent behavior from pose-estimation data. It provides data and code (on Zenodo) to help users judge how well different clustering approaches recover behavior from keypoint tracks.

title: Forestwalk: A Machine Learning Workflow Brings New Insights Into Posture and Balance in Rodent Beam Walking
one_line: ML workflow for beam-walk foot slips and posture features
details: A machine-learning workflow for the rodent beam-walk test of balance and coordination. It uses DeepLabCut keypoints of mice crossing the beam to automatically detect classic endpoints such as foot slips, then engineers a large set of posture and movement features and trains a random forest to find which features separate experimental groups. Skeletal visualizations help interpret the results in pharmacological and transgenic studies.

label: Avoidance task scoring
title: Generalization and extinction of platform-mediated avoidance in male and female rats
one_line: Open-source automated scoring for platform-mediated avoidance task.
details: An open-source scoring system for the platform-mediated avoidance task in rats. It processes DeepLabCut pose output and SimBA classifier results to quantify avoidance, freezing and darting, supporting a protocol that measures avoidance learning, generalization and extinction in one procedure.

label: Bidirectional-segmentation tracker
title: Identity-stable multi-animal tracking using bidirectional segmentation with object-level memory
one_line: Identity-stable multi-animal tracking via bidirectional segmentation with memory
details: A pipeline that corrects identity swaps in multi-animal tracking of unmarked, similar-looking animals. It runs the Cutie video object segmentation model forward and backward through a video, compares the two sets of masks, and flags only the frames where they disagree for manual review, yielding identity-consistent masks and aligned pose keypoints. It was developed on long dyadic vole recordings, extends to groups of three or more, and comes with a graphical interface.

title: IntegraPose: A unified framework for simultaneous pose estimation and behavior classification
one_line: Unified simultaneous pose estimation and behavior classification
details: An open-source framework that performs pose estimation and behavior classification together in a single model rather than as separate steps. It takes video as input and outputs both keypoints and behavior labels.

title: JAX Animal Behavior System (JABS), a genetics-informed, end-to-end advanced behavioral phenotyping platform for the laboratory mouse
one_line: Integrated hardware/software end-to-end mouse behavior phenotyping platform

title: Automated behavior classification of julius seizure mutants in Drosophila reveals stereotyped seizure stages with genotype specificity
one_line: LSTM-attention classifier of fly seizure stages
details: A deep-learning classifier that scores seizure stages in videos of bang-sensitive Drosophila mutants. It uses a long short-term memory network with an attention mechanism to label sequences as paralysis, tonic seizure, spasm, clonic seizure or recovery, enabling comparison of stage durations and transitions across genotypes and potentially high-throughput drug screening.

label: Multi-agent keypoint discovery
title: Learning Keypoints for Multi-Agent Behavior Analysis using Self-Supervision
one_line: Self-supervised keypoint discovery for multi-agent interaction videos
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
details: A self-supervised method that discovers body keypoints in videos of several interacting animals without manual keypoint labels. It uses pretrained video segmentation models to separate individuals, which helps when animals are the same species and color. The learned keypoints support downstream behavior classification and have been tested on flies, mice and rats, with generalization to ants, bees and humans.

label: 3D-printed mazes + ML tracking
title: Low-Cost 3D-Printed Mazes with Open-Source ML Tracking for Mouse Behavior
one_line: 3D-printed mazes with open-source ML tracking
details: Designs for low-cost 3D-printed mouse mazes, including a T-maze and an elevated plus maze, paired with open-source machine-learning tracking of the animals in them. The combination aims to replace commercial apparatus and tracking software for cognition and anxiety-like behavior tests while reducing setup costs.

title: The MacqD deep-learning-based model for automatic detection of socially housed laboratory macaques
one_line: Mask R-CNN Swin model detecting socially housed macaques
details: A deep-learning detector that finds and segments rhesus macaques in home-cage video. It is a modified Mask R-CNN with a Swin transformer backbone and is designed to cope with occlusion, glass reflections and overexposure in laboratory housing, including frames with two socially housed animals.

title: Marigold: a machine learning-based web app for zebrafish pose tracking
one_line: Web app for zebrafish larva pose tracking
details: A browser-based app for pose tracking of zebrafish embryos and larvae that needs no installation and runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Users label and track up to 10 keypoints in single-well or multiwell recordings through a graphical interface, and it exports kinematic measures and plots. Its compact network can train and run on ordinary computers without a dedicated GPU.

label: Second-order conditioning profiling pipeline
title: Profiling mouse behavior with computational tools to assess age-dependent differences in associative learning
one_line: Light-tone SOC paradigm plus pose/syllable analysis pipeline for associative learning.
details: A behavioral analysis pipeline built around a light-tone second-order conditioning paradigm in mice. It combines DeepLabCut pose tracking with Keypoint-MoSeq and DeepOF to break responses into behavioral syllables, revealing immobility- and escape-related actions beyond simple freezing measures and allowing comparisons across sex and age.

title: Real-time rodent behavior classifier using color-based body segmentation (R2C2)
one_line: Real-time behavior classifier via color-based body segmentation
details: A real-time behavior classifier for rodents that segments body regions by color rather than relying on keypoint pose estimation. It takes video as input and labels behavior as it is recorded.

label: Mouse head-twitch detector
title: Rapid, Open-Source, and Automated Quantification of the Head Twitch Response in C57BL/6J Mice Using DeepLabCut and Simple Behavioral Analysis
one_line: Open-source DLC+SimBA pipeline quantifying psychedelic head-twitch responses.
details: An open-source workflow for counting psychedelic-induced head-twitch responses in C57BL/6J mice from video. DeepLabCut tracks body parts and SimBA random-forest classifiers detect head twitches, removing the need for magnetometer implants or manual scoring. It was validated across different video resolutions and frame rates.

label: Subtle-change statistics
title: Statistical signature of subtle behavioral changes in large-scale assays
one_line: Statistical methods detecting subtle behavioral changes in large screens
details: A set of statistical methods for detecting subtle behavioral changes in large-scale screens of Drosophila larvae. It includes a physical model to regularize inferred larval shapes, a kernel-based test for shifts in learned behavior spaces, a generative model of behavior sequences, and suffix-tree analysis that clusters genetic lines by shared action sequences.

label: Home-cage fear tracking
title: Tracking conditioned fear in pair-housed mice using deep learning and real-time cue delivery
one_line: Home-cage paradigm with real-time cue delivery and deep-learning freezing detection.
details: A home-cage paradigm for studying conditioned fear in pair-housed mice over days. Open-source software delivers conditioned cues in real time inside the home cage while video is recorded, and a deep-learning pose model scores cue-evoked freezing across light and dark phases.

title: vassi – verifiable, automated scoring of social interactions in animal groups
one_line: Verifiable automated scoring of social interactions in groups
details: A Python package for supervised classification of directed social interactions from tracking data in individuals, pairs and larger groups. It is aimed at settings where behavior categories blend into each other and includes a validation tool to review ambiguous edge cases. It has been applied to the CALMS21 mouse resident-intruder benchmark and to groups of cichlid fish.

title: YOLO ‐Behaviour: A simple, flexible framework to automatically quantify animal behaviours from videos
one_line: YOLO-based framework to quantify animal behaviours from video
details: A framework that uses YOLO object detection models to recognize visually distinct behaviors directly from video with relatively few annotations. It supports both event-wise and frame-wise detection and has been applied to birds, zebras, giraffes and humans. Detections can also be confirmed manually in a hybrid workflow, and documentation guides users through training models on their own systems.

label: YOLOv11 repetitive-behavior scorer
title: YOLOv11-Based quantification and temporal analysis of repetitive behaviors in deer mice
one_line: YOLOv11 quantification of repetitive behaviors in deer mice
details: A YOLOv11-based approach for detecting and quantifying repetitive behaviors in deer mice from video, including their timing over a session.

title: A-SOiD, an active-learning platform for expert-guided, data-efficient discovery of behavior
one_line: Active-learning platform for data-efficient expert-guided behavior discovery
Machine-learning classifier of 3D pain behaviors using light-based image features
details: A machine-learning classifier of pain-related behaviors in mice. It works from image features captured with a light-based recording setup rather than standard pose keypoints.

label: Rat head-twitch detector
title: Assessing the effects of 5-HT2A and 5-HT5A receptor antagonists on DOI-induced head-twitch response in male rats using marker-less deep learning algorithms
one_line: Marker-less DLC+SimBA workflow detecting DOI-induced head twitches in rats.
details: A marker-less workflow for detecting DOI-induced head-twitch responses in rats from high-speed video. DeepLabCut tracks head movements and SimBA classifiers identify head twitches, avoiding surgically implanted magnets and manual counting. It was used to test serotonin receptor antagonists.

title: AutoGaitA: A versatile quantitative framework for kinematic analyses across species, perturbations and behaviours
one_line: Framework for kinematic analyses of pose data across species
details: A Python toolbox that turns pose-tracking coordinates into kinematic analyses of gait and other motor programs. It works with output from different tracking methods and supports comparisons at several levels of detail across species, behaviors and experimental perturbations, with examples in flies, mice and humans.

label: Balance beam motor scoring
title: Automated procedure to detect subtle motor alterations in the balance beam test in a mouse model of early Parkinson’s disease
one_line: Automated balance-beam analysis detecting subtle Parkinsonian motor deficits, with guide.
details: An automated procedure for the mouse balance beam test that combines DeepLabCut pose estimation with SimBA behavior classification. It extracts bout-level measures of behaviors such as walking that can reveal subtle motor deficits, demonstrated in an alpha-synuclein model of early Parkinson's disease. A step-by-step guide is provided for users without programming experience.

title: Analysis of behavioral flow resolves latent phenotypes
one_line: Behavioral flow analysis of cluster transitions plus 443-recording dataset
details: An analysis pipeline that summarizes each animal's behavior as the pattern of transitions between behavior clusters, yielding a single metric that avoids testing many clusters separately. Clusters are stabilized with machine learning so results transfer across experiments, and it works with common clustering methods. It comes with a dataset of 443 open-field recordings of mice under stress, drug and circuit manipulations.

label: Rat defensive behavior classifiers
title: Comprehensive ethological analysis of fear expression in rats using DeepLabCut and SimBA machine learning model
one_line: DLC+SimBA workflow classifying multiple rat defensive behaviors to fear cues.
details: A DeepLabCut plus SimBA workflow with machine-learning models for classifying the range of defensive behaviors rats show to fear-conditioned cues. Beyond freezing, it targets risk-assessment behaviors such as sniffing, rearing, whisking and head scanning in male and female rats.

label: Facial affect scorer
title: Deep Learning Scoring of Negative Affect from Mouse Facial Expressions
one_line: Deep learning scoring of negative affect from facial expressions
details: A deep-learning approach for scoring negative affect from video of mouse facial expressions. It is trained on weakly labeled video from lipopolysaccharide-injected and control mice and scores collections of frames rather than single images to reduce label noise.

title: Ethome: tools for machine learning of animal behavior
one_line: Toolkit converting pose and annotations to features and classifiers
venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
details: A Python toolkit for machine learning of animal behavior. It reads pose-tracking files and behavior annotations, builds feature tables, interpolates tracking data and trains behavior classifiers.

title: EthoWatcher OS: improving the reproducibility and quality of categorical and morphologic/kinematic data from behavioral recordings in laboratory animals
one_line: Open software for categorical and kinematic behavioral recording
details: Open-source software for recording and analyzing behavior in laboratory animals. It supports both categorical behavior scoring and morphological or kinematic measurements from recordings, with an emphasis on reproducibility and data quality.

title: Hierarchical behavioral analysis framework as a platform for standardized quantitative identification of behaviors
one_line: Hierarchical framework creating spontaneous behavior atlas for mice
details: A hierarchical framework that organizes high-dimensional behavioral data from freely moving mice into behavior modules and their transitions. It was used to build an atlas of spontaneous behavior in male and female mice and to derive simple measures, such as the sniffing-to-grooming ratio, for rapidly assessing behavioral state.

label: Spatial-temporal window transformer
title: Hierarchical Spatial–Temporal Window Transformer for Pose-Based Rodent Behavior Recognition
one_line: Pose-based transformer for rodent behavior recognition
venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
details: A transformer network that recognizes rodent behaviors, including interactions between multiple animals, from pose keypoints. It learns features over windows of space and time without a predefined skeleton and was evaluated on the CRIM13 and CalMS21 datasets.

label: Marmoset behavior dataset
title: High-throughput unsupervised quantification of patterns in the natural behavior of marmosets
one_line: Multimodal dataset and unsupervised behavior quantification in marmosets
details: A multimodal dataset from a large cohort of marmoset monkeys, with code for unsupervised quantification of their natural home-cage behavior. It describes typical behavior patterns, their relation to cagemates and colony vocalizations, and uses outlier detection to flag atypical responses to novel, appetitive, aversive and social stimuli.

label: Photometry-behavior state-space framework
title: Identifying behavioral links to neural dynamics of multifiber photometry recordings in a mouse social behavior network
one_line: State-space latent variable framework linking multifiber photometry to social behaviors.
details: A state-space analysis framework that relates multi-fiber photometry calcium signals to mouse social behavior. It fits latent variable models, including a linear dynamical system and a hidden semi-Markov model, to recordings during aggression and mating to find interpretable neural states linked to behavior.

label: Territorial behavior assay
title: Induction of territorial behavior and dominance hierarchies in laboratory mice
one_line: Protocol inducing territoriality with simultaneous urine-marking tracking in mouse pairs.
details: A protocol for inducing territorial behavior and dominance hierarchies in pairs of laboratory mice in small enclosures. It includes a method for tracking urine-marking behavior of both mice simultaneously alongside attacks and chases.

title: Lightning Pose: improved animal pose estimation via semi-supervised learning, Bayesian ensembling and cloud-native open-source tools
one_line: Semi-supervised pose estimation with Bayesian ensembling and cloud-native tooling

label: Cockroach ML teaching pipeline
title: Low-Cost Approaches in Neuroscience to Teach Machine Learning Using a Cockroach Model
one_line: Low-cost SLEAP/Colab pipeline teaching ML behavior analysis with cockroaches.
details: An educational, low-cost program for teaching machine-learning behavior analysis using cockroaches on a linear-track place-preference task. Students track animals with SLEAP running in Google Colab, then derive distance, velocity and zone times and cluster the coordinates into behaviors, without needing expensive hardware.

title: Mamba-MSQNet: A Fast and Efficient Model for Animal Action Recognition
one_line: Efficient Mamba-based model for multi-species animal action recognition
venue: IEEE International Workshop on Metrology for Agriculture and Forestry
details: A deep-learning model for recognizing animal actions across many species from video. It replaces parts of the transformer-based MSQNet with selective state-space (Mamba) layers to cut parameters and compute, and was evaluated on the Animal Kingdom dataset.

title: Characterizing the structure of mouse behavior using Motion Sequencing
one_line: Protocol for Motion Sequencing to parse behavior into syllables

title: High quality, high throughput, and low-cost simultaneous video recording of 60 animals in operant chambers using PiRATeMC
one_line: Raspberry Pi system recording 60 operant chambers simultaneously
details: A Raspberry Pi-based video recording system scaled up to capture 60 rats simultaneously in individual operant chambers, such as drug self-administration boxes. It provides synchronized recording across devices with small file sizes at a fraction of commercial costs, and can be customized for other species and settings.

title: PrecisionTrack: A Platform for Automated Long-Term Social Behavior Analysis in Naturalized Environments
one_line: Platform for long-term multi-animal tracking and social behavior analysis in naturalized environments
details: An integrated, open-source framework for tracking groups of interacting mice over long periods in naturalistic, crowded arenas while keeping individual identities stable through occlusions. It runs in real time and adds a transformer-based action recognizer (MART) for per-animal behavior labels plus a graph-network module (G-MART) that infers who is interacting with whom. Outputs include social interaction networks that can be followed across time, and documented workflows let users train custom pipelines for other species.

label: Social-role model
title: Quantifying social roles in multi-animal videos using subject-aware deep-learning
one_line: Subject-aware deep learning identifying social roles in multi-animal videos
details: A subject-aware deep-learning approach, released as LabGym2, that classifies the behavior of each individual in a group of two or more animals while taking its social partners and surroundings into account. It works from video and assigns social roles to freely moving individuals, and has been applied across species from insects in partner-preference assays to primates in the field. The open-source software emphasizes interpretable, controllable classification of interactive behavior.

title: Long-term tracking of social structure in groups of rats
one_line: Long-term automated tracking of group social hierarchy over 250 days
details: Open-source tracking software for continuously monitoring groups of rats over very long periods, used to follow individual behavior and the formation of group dominance hierarchies over more than 250 days. It supports analysis of how social structure changes when group membership or the arena changes, and is aimed at studying social behavior in more naturalistic, group-housed settings rather than isolated pairwise tests.

title: A study of animal action segmentation algorithms across supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised learning paradigms
one_line: Benchmarks action segmentation paradigms; introduces semi-supervised model
venue: Neurons Behavior Data analysis and Theory
details: A semi-supervised switching linear dynamical system for action segmentation, introduced alongside a systematic comparison of supervised, unsupervised and semi-supervised methods for labeling each video frame with discrete behaviors. The model combines ideas from supervised neural networks and unsupervised graphical models, and the comparison spans fly, mouse and human datasets. Code is open source and builds on the daart segmentation package; it is useful for choosing a segmentation approach for pose or feature time series.

title: An integrative assay for measuring social aversion and motivation in freely behaving mice
one_line: Behavioral assay measuring social aversion and motivation
details: An open behavioral assay (selective access to unrestricted social interaction) for measuring social aversion in freely behaving mice by combining measures of social motivation, hesitancy and free interaction in one task. It has been used to show isolation- and stress-induced social aversion, and its video recordings are compatible with deep-learning behavior analysis pipelines. Design files and resources are openly shared.

title: Multi-animal 3D social pose estimation, identification and behaviour embedding with a few-shot learning framework
one_line: Few-shot multi-animal 3D pose, identification and social behavior embedding
details: An open-source framework (Social Behavior Atlas) for multi-animal 3D pose estimation that requires relatively few labeled frames, identifies individuals without identity labels, and uses unsupervised learning to embed and classify social behavior. It takes multi-camera video of interacting animals, was demonstrated mainly on mice including autism-model knockouts, and can be applied to other species with custom datasets.

label: Rare-behavior search
title: Sifting Through the Haystack - Efficiently Finding Rare Animal Behaviors in Large-Scale Datasets
one_line: Finding rare behaviors in large video datasets with little annotation effort
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
details: An open-source pipeline for finding rare behaviors in long recordings so that training sets for rare-behavior classifiers can be built with little annotation effort. It takes unlabeled pose or accelerometer data, scores samples with a graph-based anomaly detection model, and directs human labeling toward the most unusual segments while treating the rest as routine. It makes no assumptions about which rare behaviors are present and was tested on lab and field datasets from several species.

title: Sphynx: An Automated Behavioral Analysis Tool for Neuronal Selectivity Identification
one_line: Behavior segmentation tool for identifying neuronal selectivity
details: A software tool that extracts a broad set of behavioral variables from video of mice and segments ongoing behavior into discrete acts linked to features of the environment. It is designed to be paired with neural recordings so that researchers can identify neurons selective to particular behaviors or contexts.

title: Segmentation tracking and clustering system enables accurate multi-animal tracking of social behaviors
one_line: Segmentation tracking and clustering for multi-animal social behavior
details: An open-source segmentation-based system for tracking and estimating the pose of multiple mice during close social interactions, paired with a weakly supervised clustering method that uses genotype information to reveal interpretable behavioral differences. It has a modular, web-based design that makes it straightforward to swap in newer computer vision models and run analyses as a service, even from a laptop. A long-term multi-animal tracking dataset accompanies the tool.

title: SUBTLE: An Unsupervised Platform with Temporal Link Embedding that Maps Animal Behavior
one_line: Spectrogram-UMAP temporal link embedding for unsupervised behavior mapping
details: An open-source unsupervised behavior-mapping framework that takes 3D skeleton (keypoint) data, converts it to spectrograms, and embeds it with UMAP in a way that preserves temporal relationships between frames. Clustering the embedding recovers behaviors such as walking, grooming, standing and rearing and can reveal subtle group differences, for example by age. It was developed on mouse data.

title: SuperAnimal pretrained pose estimation models for behavioral analysis
one_line: Pretrained pose models for many species usable without labeling (DeepLabCut model zoo)

title: TIBA: A web application for the visual analysis of temporal occurrences, interactions, and transitions of animal behavior
one_line: Web app visualizing temporal occurrences, interactions, transitions of behavior
details: An open-source web application (The Interactive Behavior Analyzer) for visualizing behavioral event data exported from common event-logging software. It produces interactive plots of when behaviors occur, networks showing the number and direction of interactions between individuals, and behavioral transition diagrams, and lets users compare transitions across datasets. It runs in the browser, needs no programming, and works for any species.

label: Pharmacology pose toolkit
title: A Pharmacology Toolkit for Animal Pose Estimation, Tracking and Analysis
one_line: Computer vision counting crossing, rearing, grooming in open field
venue: International Mobile, Intelligent, and Ubiquitous Computing Conference
details: An open-source computer vision toolkit for scoring mouse open-field experiments, aimed at pharmacology studies. It combines deep-learning detection, distance-based matching for tracking several mice, and image processing to count line crossings, rearing and grooming from video.

title: AmadeusGPT: a natural language interface for interactive animal behavioral analysis
one_line: Natural-language interface that writes and runs behavior analysis code

title: Automated maternal behavior during early life in rodents (AMBER) pipeline
one_line: Pipeline for automated scoring of maternal dam-pup behavior

title: BAMBI: A new method for automated assessment of bidirectional early-life interaction between maternal behavior and pup vocalization in mouse dam-pup dyads
one_line: Automated assessment of dam behavior and pup vocalization interaction
details: An automated version of the pup retrieval test (Bidirectional Automated Mother-pup Behavioral Interaction) that synchronously records video of the dam and ultrasonic vocalizations from the pups. It scores retrieval and vocalization parameters together so the two-way interaction between mother and pup can be assessed in the home cage. Materials are openly shared and target studies of early-life social development in mice.

title: Relax, it doesn't matter how you get there: A new self-supervised approach for multi-timescale behavior analysis
one_line: Self-supervised multi-timescale behavior representations (Bootstrap Across Multiple Scales)
details: An open-source self-supervised method (Bootstrap Across Multiple Scales) that learns representations of behavior from trajectory or pose data without labels. It trains on predicting future actions and keeps separate latent spaces for short- and long-term dynamics, so the embeddings capture both moment-to-moment and slower behavioral factors. The learned features can be reused for many downstream tasks and were evaluated on the MABe 2022 multi-agent mouse and fly benchmark.

title: Automatically annotated motion tracking identifies a distinct social behavioral profile following chronic social defeat stress
one_line: Supervised and unsupervised social behavior profiling from DLC pose data

label: Balance-beam ataxia pipeline
title: Detecting ataxia using an automated analysis of motor coordination and balance of mice on the balance beam
one_line: Open-source pipeline quantifying coordination and slips on balance beam
details: An open-source pipeline and low-cost build guide for automating the mouse balance beam test of motor coordination. MATLAB scripts with FFmpeg and ImageJ preprocess videos and extract beam crossing time, mice are tracked with motr, and a trained JAABA classifier detects stops and missteps. It is intended for ataxia and neurodegeneration models and replaces manual scoring.

label: Synthetic rodent behavior dataset
title: Disentangling rodent behaviors to improve automated behavior recognition
one_line: Synthetic dataset isolating hard behavior dynamics for recognition models
details: An open-source synthetic dataset and generator of artificial behavior data that isolates aspects of rodent behavior dynamics known to be hard for automated recognition models. Because the data are generated, labels are unlimited and noise-free, making it useful for testing and improving behavior recognition architectures rather than for analyzing real recordings.

title: LabGym: Quantification of user-defined animal behaviors using learning-based holistic assessment
one_line: Holistic learning-based quantification of user-defined animal behaviors

label: Wet-dog shake classifier
title: Multi-view image-based behavior classification of wet-dog shake in Kainate rat model
one_line: Multi-view image classification detecting wet-dog shake behavior
details: A multi-view, image-based classification system that detects wet-dog shakes, a brief whole-body shaking behavior relevant to seizure, withdrawal and other rat disease models. It fuses video frames across time and from one or more cameras without hand-crafted features, and adding camera views improves detection. It was developed in a kainate rat model and could be adapted to other behaviors.

title: OpenApePose, a database of annotated ape photographs for pose estimation
one_line: Annotated ape photograph database for pose estimation
details: An open dataset of tens of thousands of photographs of six ape species (including chimpanzees, bonobos, gorillas, orangutans and gibbons) in naturalistic settings, each annotated with 16 body landmarks. It is intended for training and benchmarking pose estimation models for apes, and models trained on it track apes better than those trained on monkey or human data.

title: SAMPL is a high-throughput solution to study unconstrained vertical behavior in small animals
one_line: High-throughput apparatus and analysis for unconstrained vertical behavior
details: A scalable, open apparatus with real-time open-source software for measuring posture and locomotion of small animals as they move vertically in an unconstrained way. It supports larval zebrafish, fruit flies and C. elegans, is built for high-throughput genetic or drug screens, and outputs kinematic measures of balance and navigation.

title: Automatic mapping of multiplexed social receptive fields by deep learning and GPU-accelerated 3D videography
one_line: 3D multi-animal tracking with GPU optimization mapping social receptive fields
details: An open-source hardware and software system that tracks the 3D posture of multiple unmarked, interacting mice by combining 3D videography, deep learning, a physical body model, and GPU-accelerated optimization. It works in complete darkness and alongside electrophysiology, and includes a statistical model linking 3D social behavior to neural activity to map the social receptive fields of neurons.

title: AlphaTracker: a multi-animal tracking and behavioral analysis tool
one_line: Multi-animal tracking and behavioral analysis pipeline with low hardware needs

label: Automated pup retrieval scoring
title: Automated procedure to assess pup retrieval in laboratory mice
one_line: Machine-learning procedure to automatically assess pup retrieval test performance.
details: A step-by-step protocol for automatically scoring the mouse pup retrieval test of maternal care. It tracks the dam and a pup from video with DeepLabCut and then uses SimBA classifiers to detect maternal approach, carrying and digging, from which retrieval success is estimated, replacing manual scoring.

title: Self-Supervised Keypoint Discovery in Behavioral Videos
one_line: Self-supervised keypoint discovery from unlabelled behavioral videos
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
details: An open-source self-supervised method (Behavioral Keypoint Discovery) that finds keypoints on behaving animals directly from unlabeled video by learning to reconstruct the movement between frames. No manual keypoint annotation is needed, and the discovered keypoints correspond to meaningful body parts that can be used for downstream tasks such as behavior classification. It was shown on mice, flies, jellyfish and humans.

label: Fear conditioning analysis tool
title: Behavior analysis tool for fear conditioning paradigm
one_line: Software tool for analyzing animal behavior in fear conditioning experiments
details: A software tool for extracting measures of animal behavior from video recordings of rodents in fear conditioning experiments.

title: BehaviorDEPOT is a simple, flexible tool for automated behavioral detection based on markerless pose tracking
one_line: Rule-based automated behavior detection from markerless pose tracking

title: ConstrastivePose: A contrastive learning approach for self-supervised feature engineering for pose estimation and behavorial classification of interacting animals
one_line: Contrastive self-supervised features from pose for behavior classification
details: An open-source method that uses contrastive self-supervised learning on pose estimation data to learn features for behavior classification. It uses unlabeled videos to learn representations of interacting animals, reducing the need for hand-crafted pose features and large labeled training sets. The learned features then feed standard supervised classifiers and were demonstrated on mouse social interaction data.

title: "Corvid Tracking Studio": A custom-built motion capture system to track head movements of corvids.
one_line: Custom motion-capture system tracking corvid head movements
details: A custom-built infrared motion-capture room for tracking fast 3D head movements of freely moving large-billed crows that can interact with other birds and objects. Reflective markers on the head are tracked by infrared cameras, and a calibration step reconstructs the positions of the eyes and beak tip to estimate head orientation, for example during saccadic head movements.

title: EXPLORE: a novel deep learning-based analysis method for exploration behaviour in object recognition tests
one_line: CNN pipeline scoring object exploration in recognition tests
details: An open-source pipeline for scoring object exploration in rodent object recognition memory tests. A convolutional neural network trained on user-labeled examples classifies behavior near objects directly from video images instead of relying on tracked points, so users decide which interactions count as exploration. A set of graphical interfaces covers the whole analysis without programming or deep-learning expertise.

title: Protocol for non-invasive assessment of spontaneous movements of group-housed animals using remote video monitoring
one_line: Low-cost infrared home-cage video monitoring system with deep-learning tracking
details: An open protocol for building a low-cost, remotely accessible infrared video system that monitors group-housed mice in their home cages without human presence. The recorded video is analyzed with deep-learning networks to track unmarked animals and quantify spontaneous movement, and the setup can be adapted to other home-cage designs and species.

title: OpenLabCluster: active learning based clustering and classification of animal behaviors based on kinematic body keypoints
one_line: Active-learning clustering and classification of keypoint behaviors

title: PyRAT: An Open-Source Python Library for Animal Behavior Analysis
one_line: Python library analyzing tracking data, clustering behaviors, occupancy

title: A Layered, Hybrid Machine Learning Analytic Workflow for Mouse Risk Assessment Behavior
one_line: Layered RF+HMM hybrid model to quantify risk assessment behavior
details: An open-source layered machine-learning workflow that combines random forest and hidden Markov model predictions from DeepLabCut pose features, then passes them through further HMM layers (reHMM and reHMM+). The approach adds temporal structure to frame-wise classifiers while keeping states human-interpretable. It was developed to quantify mouse risk assessment behavior in response to predator odors and other chemosensory stimuli.

label: Neonatal mouse withdrawal tracking
title: Rodent Tracking and Abnormal Behavior Classification in Live Video using Deep Neural Networks
one_line: Compares pretrained backbones for tracking neonatal mice in opioid withdrawal.
venue: IEEE Symposium Series on Computational Intelligence
details: A study comparing pretrained backbone networks (ResNet, MobileNet, EfficientNet) within DeepLabCut for tracking the nose, ears and tail base of neonatal mice in video. It is aimed at assessing behavior in pups undergoing opioid withdrawal, with tracking serving as the first step toward detecting abnormal withdrawal behavior.

title: SLEAP: A deep learning system for multi-animal pose tracking
one_line: Deep learning multi-animal pose tracking system

label: Pigeon behavior classifier
title: Supervised machine learning aided behavior classification in pigeons
one_line: Open-source package building supervised behavior classifiers for pigeons.
details: An open-source package that builds supervised machine-learning and deep-learning classifiers for pigeon behaviors from pose estimation output such as DeepLabCut keypoints. It treats the pose data as multivariate time series, classifies a set of distinct behaviors, and includes an option to bias predictions toward precision or recall. It is designed to be extendable to other bird species.

label: Occluded-rat identity tracker
title: Tracking Highly Similar Rat Instances under Heavy Occlusions: An Unsupervised Deep Generative Pipeline
one_line: Generative-model identity tracking and segmentation of occluded similar rats
details: An open-source pipeline of deep generative models for keeping track of identity and segmenting individual animals that look alike, such as unmarked white rats, even when they heavily occlude one another. It relies on edge information to separate touching animals and is trained on synthetically generated data, so no manual annotation is needed. It works on overhead laboratory video of groups of rats.

title: Identifying behavioral structure from deep variational embeddings of animal motion
one_line: Unsupervised variational embeddings segment pose into hierarchical behavioral motifs

title: The Multi-Agent Behavior Dataset: Mouse Dyadic Social Interactions
one_line: Annotated multi-agent mouse social interaction benchmark dataset
details: An open benchmark dataset (Caltech Mouse Social Interactions) of tracked pose trajectories from pairs of freely behaving mice in a resident-intruder assay, with millions of unlabeled frames and over a million frames with frame-level behavior annotations. It defines tasks for evaluating behavior classifiers, including learning differences between annotators and learning new behaviors from few labels.

title: DeepEthogram, a machine learning pipeline for supervised behavior classification from raw pixels
one_line: Supervised classification of behaviors directly from raw video pixels

title: DeepLabStream enables closed-loop behavioral experiments using deep learning-based markerless, real-time posture detection
one_line: Closed-loop experiments via real-time markerless posture detection

label: Annotation-difference analysis
title: Interpreting Expert Annotation Differences in Animal Behavior
one_line: Program synthesis interpreting differences between expert behavior annotators
details: A method that uses program synthesis to explain how different experts annotate the same behaviors differently. Working from animal trajectory features, it learns small interpretable programs that select relevant features and temporal filters reflecting what each annotator emphasizes, and it was evaluated on mouse social behavior data. It aims to make behavior annotations more reproducible.

title: Quantitative standardization of resident mouse behavior for studies of aggression and social defeat
one_line: Standardization of resident mouse behavior for aggression/defeat studies
details: An approach for standardizing and quantifying the behavior of resident mice used in aggression and social defeat studies, so that the aggressor side of these paradigms can be measured consistently.

title: The Mouse Action Recognition System (MARS) software pipeline for automated analysis of social behaviors in mice
one_line: Pipeline for pose and social behavior classification in mice

title: The PAIR-R24M Dataset for Multi-animal 3D Pose Estimation
one_line: Multi-animal 3D pose estimation dataset of interacting rats
details: An open dataset for multi-animal 3D pose estimation containing millions of frames of multi-view RGB video of pairs of interacting rats, synchronized with 3D motion capture ground truth. It covers many rat pairs and camera viewpoints, includes behavior and interaction labels for benchmarking, and comes with a multi-animal baseline built on DANNCE.

title: Partitioning variability in animal behavioral videos using semi-supervised variational autoencoders
one_line: Semi-supervised VAE partitioning video variability into supervised and latent factors
details: An open-source semi-supervised variational autoencoder (partitioned subspace VAE, part of the BehaveNet package) that combines pose estimates such as DeepLabCut output with unsupervised dimensionality reduction of the raw video. It splits behavioral video into interpretable components tied to tracked body parts plus additional latent factors that pose alone misses. It was demonstrated on head-fixed and freely moving mouse video and supports downstream behavioral and neural analyses.

label: Semi-supervised segmentation model
title: Semi-supervised sequence modeling for improved behavioral segmentation
one_line: Semi-supervised sequence modeling for behavioral segmentation
details: An open-source semi-supervised sequence model (daart) for segmenting behavioral features from video, such as pose time series, into discrete behaviors like walking or grooming. Training combines a few hand labels, easy-to-compute heuristic labels, and self-supervised prediction of future features, so unlabeled frames improve accuracy when hand labels are sparse.

label: Pup retrieval movement dataset
title: Systematic analysis of goal‐related movement sequences during maternal behaviour in a female mouse model for Rett syndrome
one_line: Manually curated gold-standard dataset of goal-related movements during pup retrieval.
details: A manually curated, frame-by-frame annotated dataset of goal-related movement sequences during pup retrieval by female mice, comparing wild-type animals with a Mecp2 heterozygous model of Rett syndrome across several days and strains. Annotations were made in DataVyu and are intended as a reference for building machine-learning behavioral repertoires of maternal behavior.

title: Task Programming: Learning Data Efficient Behavior Representations
one_line: Self-supervised behavior representations from expert-programmed tasks for data efficiency
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
details: An open-source self-supervised method (TREBA) that learns trajectory embeddings for behavior analysis from tracked pose data. Domain experts write a few short programs that compute behavioral attributes, and the model learns representations by predicting them, which reduces how many manually annotated frames are needed to train classifiers. It was evaluated on mouse and fruit fly datasets.

label: DLC vs commercial benchmark
title: Deep learning-based behavioral analysis reaches human accuracy and is capable of outperforming commercial solutions
one_line: Annotated video dataset benchmarking DLC versus commercial systems
details: An open set of mouse videos from the open field, elevated plus maze and forced swim tests annotated by several human raters, together with the R-based DLCAnalyzer code. It was used to compare DeepLabCut pose tracking plus supervised classifiers against commercial systems (EthoVision XT and TSE), and the workflow scores ethologically relevant behaviors from pose data. It is a reference for validating pose-based scoring of classic rodent tests.

title: Deep-learning-based identification, tracking, pose estimation and behaviour classification of interacting primates and mice in complex environments
one_line: Deep learning identification, tracking, pose and behavior classification of interacting animals
